content:
maria: Quick heads-up — saw a p99 blowup during last night's 10m burst on rtf-prod. Autoscaler added pods but tail latency jumped ~2.8x. Suspect kernel handoff + KV cold misses.

ajay: timeline? any correlated deploys or kernel flips?

maria: no deploys. timeline: 02:14–02:24 UTC burst from marketing test traffic. Autoscaler scaleup at 02:16, new pods ready ~02:19, p95 stayed ok but p99 jumps at 02:17–02:20.

perf-bot: [alert] p99 latency > 1200ms for model/gptx-3-quantized between 02:17–02:20 UTC; KV cache miss rate increased from 4% to 37%.

jonathan: can you post a flamegraph or profile from the p99 sample window? curious if kernel selection overhead is the culprit or queueing path.

li: uploaded profiles -> https://console.redwood/profiles/2219876543/flare (link)

li: short summary from profile: when new pods join, we do kernel probe for best matrix-mul variant. Probe path runs a small calibration with 3 sequences, CPU-bound compilation for 120–250ms on the new node before it accepts traffic. That lines up with scaleup window.

ajay: so we have 2 contributors: kernel probe latency on warmup + KV cache misses causing long token generation. Any batching differences? microbatch sizes?

maria: yes — autoscaler sends traffic to new nodes which have empty KV caches. We observed microbatch average size drop from 6 -> 2 for the affected requests (burst client has low parallelism). Smaller microbatches amplify per-request overheads + miss penalty.

jonathan: interesting. Did the kernel probe change recently? I thought we switched to nonblocking probe last month.

li: probe code changed to async in commit 76b9 but we still run a blocking JIT-compile step for certain kernel variants on first use. On the new nodes the probe picks a slower kernel first, triggers fallback, then compiles the faster one -> double penalty.

maria: repro script I ran locally:
```bash
# simulate burst with low concurrency to force small microbatches
wrk -c 4 -t 2 -d 60s https://rtf-prod/generate?model=gptx-3-quantized
```
Results: p99 ~ 1.1s on cold node vs 320ms on warmed node. KV miss delta ~30%.

ajay: sounds like two knobs: 1) avoid blocking kernel compile on request path (defer/compile-on-idle) 2) prevent immediate routing to completely cold nodes during tight SLO windows (runway or ramp).

sre-oncall: autoscaler note — we currently have aggressive target latency SLO = 200ms and min-burst capacity = 0. We could set a brief runway (reserve 1 warm pod) for prod during marketing windows.

jonathan: also consider probe ordering change: prefer fast portable kernel variant (even if slightly lower throughput) until KV warms. That reduces worst-case latency.

li: experiment idea: change probe to prefer stable fallback kernel and schedule async compilation of optimized kernels at lower priority. I can prototype a patch.

maria: other mitigation: increase batching window by 10–15ms during burst detection to push microbatch sizes from 2->4. Tradeoff: slight p50 increase but lower p99. Worth it?

ajay: yes, that's the classic p50 vs p99 trade. Let's A/B it. We can add a runtime flag: batch_wait_ms_burst = 15.

perf-bot: experiment created -> /experiments/rtf-burst-batchwait-221987 (auto-tracking).

jonathan: for rollout plan:
- short-term (hotfix): autoscaler runway = 1 warm pod for prod during scheduled bursts
- mid-term: change probe ordering + async compile off critical path
- experiment: batch_wait_ms_burst = 15 A/B for 2 weeks

maria: I'll open a PR for autoscaler runway config + test harness for warm-routing. Li, can you start the probe-change branch?

li: on it. branch: kernel-probe-softstart-221987. Will mock compile latency in CI so we don't regress.

ajay: please add a small distrib trace example to the PR showing kernel probe span and kv:miss span. Makes review easier.

maria: noted. Also adding a synthetic smoke that simulates burst+low-concurrency to our nightly perf gate.

sre-oncall: I'll schedule a temporary runway change for next marketing test and monitor p99.

jonathan: great — we should capture before/after p50/p95/p99, kv hit-rate, avg microbatch size, and number of kernel compilations during window.

maria: thanks all. keeping this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
